rationale_first_sentence: Every prostate MRI must be checked against PI-QUAL v2 quality criteria before the biopsy pathway is decided (Q4a median 9, Q4b median 8 — consensus agree); a quality-assured scan — 1.5T or 3T, biparametric without routine contrast-enhanced sequences — is acceptable (Q1, Q5-Q7 median 8), and MRI that fails quality standards must not gate the biopsy decision.

For an indeterminate lesion (PI-RADS 3), ProBIOPSY endorses PSAD as the primary gate to reduce unnecessary biopsies — for bpMRI (Q11 median 7) and even more strongly for mpMRI (Q14 median 8) — whereas PSMA PET and microultrasound remain conditional options rather than standard workup (Q18, Q21).

When MRI is negative but clinical suspicion remains high (abnormal DRE, persistently elevated PSA, strong family history, Black ethnicity, or prior negative biopsy), a 12-core systematic biopsy is still endorsed (Q25 median 7 — consensus agree; Q55a median 7) and PSMA PET may serve as an ancillary test (Q19 median 8 — consensus agree).

ProBIOPSY explicitly rejects PSMA PET/MRI as an upfront first-line biopsy-decision tool (Q17 median 2 — consensus disagree) and microultrasound as an upfront alternative to prostate MRI (Q20 median 2 — consensus disagree); both modalities have defined ancillary niches but must not replace quality-assured MRI at triage.
ProBIOPSY endorses AI software as an aid to MRI lesion detection and characterization, with interpretation remaining the radiologist's responsibility (Q26 median 7 — consensus agree).

ProBIOPSY endorses a reduced (6-core) systematic scheme in advanced disease, where detection of any grade group confirms management rather than changing mapping precision (Q57 median 8 — consensus agree).

ProBIOPSY endorses the 12-core systematic template as the standard when systematic cores are indicated (Q52 median 8 — consensus agree) and rejects the classical 6-core sextant template (Q51 median 3), the Ginsburg 4-6 core template (Q53 median 3) and saturation biopsy (Q54 median 2) — all by consensus disagree.

ProBIOPSY reached no consensus on a fixed targeted-core count: adapting the number of targeted cores to PI-RADS score was rated 'neither' (Q34 median 6) and the proposed minimum of 3 cores per target failed to reach consensus in both rounds (Q35, Q36), so the system reports core count as an open option rather than enforcing a fixed number.

ProBIOPSY adopts the term 'perilesional biopsy' for cores placed just outside the MRI lesion margin (Q37a — SOQ consensus), requires targeted cores to be placed within 10 mm of the lesion (Q38 — SOQ consensus) and scales the number of perilesional cores to lesion size (Q39 median 7 — consensus agree), with a maximum of 2 cores per large lesion (Q41 — SOQ consensus).

For a unifocal lesion, ProBIOPSY endorses targeted + perilesional biopsy without contralateral systematic cores (Q43 median 7 — consensus agree) and bilateral targeted+perilesional schemes for multifocal bilateral disease (Q49 median 7 — consensus agree), while adding full systematic biopsy to a targeted+perilesional scheme is rejected (Q45 median 3 — consensus disagree).

ProBIOPSY endorses the transperineal route as the standard for prostate biopsy (Q58 — SOQ consensus) with periprostatic nerve block for both transrectal (Q59) and transperineal (Q60) approaches (both SOQ consensus).

ProBIOPSY links biopsy scheme to downstream treatment intent: for focal therapy, targeted+perilesional alone is deemed insufficient and contralateral systematic biopsy must be added (Q65 median 7 — consensus agree), whereas nerve sparing, whole-gland radiotherapy, focal boost and ADT-duration planning are adequately served by targeted+perilesional schemes (Q67, Q70, Q79, Q85, Q88, Q91, Q94 median 7-8).

Infection risk factors (Q62 catalogue: immunosuppression, prior prostatitis, recent instrumentation, MRSA colonization) escalate the perioperative rule R11 — prefer the transperineal route and augmented prophylaxis when transrectal access is unavoidable.
Patients unfit for curative treatment shift the goal from mapping precision to confirmation — R06 reduced systematic scheme applies.
Prior negative biopsy with persisting suspicion raises sepsis risk on repeat access and keeps the 12-core template relevant (R03/R11 escalation).
Abnormal DRE with negative MRI keeps clinical suspicion high — systematic 12-core biopsy per R03.
